blocks.heading: What this section covers
blocks.text: Use a range of vocabulary, sentence structures and literary features chosen for their effect, all controlled; write clearly and coherently with a range of language you can command.

blocks.heading: Precision and range
blocks.text: The precise word names the exact thing; the general word gestures at a family of things, and the difference is what the reader has to work with. A range of language means varied vocabulary, sentence structures and literary features — all controlled: range is measured in what the writing keeps accurate, not in what it attempts. The syllabus asks for ideas expressed clearly, coherently and accurately with an appropriate range — which is the whole of this topic in one line, and the writing marks in both papers rest on it.

blocks.heading: Worked example: the precise word at work
blocks.text: Take "the animal moved quickly across the road". The general word gestures at a family of animals and a family of movements; the precise word names the thing — "the jackal trotted across the road", and now the reader sees one animal doing one thing at one speed, and the sentence has stopped being a description and become a sighting. Precision is a service to the reader: every exact noun is one the reader does not have to build.

blocks.heading: Control before complexity
blocks.text: Control comes before complexity because the range is judged inside accuracy: a sentence the writer can hold is worth ten the writer cannot, and the table rewards expression the writer keeps command of. A varied range of sentences means different shapes held deliberately — simple, compound, complex, minor, fronted — each chosen for its effect; long complex sentences in which the grammar breaks down are range attempted and lost, and the reader is lost in the same place.

blocks.heading: Worked example: two sentences, one choice
blocks.text: Watch a writer choose between range and control at the level of one sentence. Ambition: "The thunder, which had been circling the valley all afternoon like a debt collector, finally arrived with the rain." Control: "The thunder had circled the valley all afternoon. When it arrived, it came with the rain." The first is fine — held, punctuated, the simile earning its clause — and a writer who can hold it should. The second is the same content in two shapes the writer can hold at speed, under time, tired. The range is real in both; the difference is the price of each on a writing day, and knowing your own handwriting’s speed is part of knowing your range.

blocks.heading: Ambition without command
blocks.text: Ambitious vocabulary used in the wrong sense, or informality that slides into error, costs the accuracy the range was meant to serve: an unusual word must be a word the writer can use, not just find. "The sunset was ephemeral at six and very nice by seven" has spent its ambition on the wrong half of the sentence; the reader who knows the word winces, and the reader who does not is misled. The rule is simple and unsparing: use the range you own, own the range you use, and add words to the owned set by checking each new one before it carries a sentence.

blocks.heading: Clarity and coherence
blocks.text: Writing clearly and coherently means the reader follows the sentences without re-reading them: clarity is the sentence’s work being done, and coherence the paragraph’s. Clarity is won at the level of the sentence — the subject where the reader expects it, the verb where the sentence needs it — and coherence at the level of the paragraph, where each sentence hands the next its subject. Neither is a style: they are the minimum the reader is owed, and the range rides on top of them, never instead of them.
